data.narrative:
The Nuclear Company is a Series A-stage nuclear energy venture that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation exercise compares the target against a comp universe of 3 public entities and 8 private companies in the nuclear energy sector, including same-stage and adjacent-stage peers such as Fuse Energy ($200M Series A valuation), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M Seed valuation), and Valar Atomics ($6.0B Series B valuation).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a standard 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis derives valuation from the median across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, producing $808M. The peer range spans $200M to $6.0B, reflecting substantial heterogeneity in this early-stage sector.

The triangulated valuation range is $85M to $929M, with a median of $454M. The width of this range reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage venture valuation and heterogeneity within the nuclear energy peer set. Stage-progression implies a more conservative floor, while peer-median valuation—anchored to Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M—suggests substantially higher value. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to the peer set, capital efficiency to next inflection, and regulatory pathway clarity for the specific reactor technology.
